record: cost basis for rung 5, prepared 2026-11-16 from measured generation time, awaiting signature
basis: measured adapter generation on this checkout: 37.83 s per item at cap 512 over 50 items (outputs/benchmark_v2/eval/generation_512.json); corroborated by 36.51 s per item at cap 512 over 20 items (outputs/benchmark_v2/eval/decode_speed.json). A, C, D and M perform no language-model call; C and M are assembled from an adapter generation, so each carries that generation's cost once.
derivation: 37.83 s/item x 520 items = 19671.6 s per pass; identical for every cell whose text needs the adapter
reading: rung 5 separates the model cells (B, C, M: about 5.5 h of generation per pass) from the assemblers (A, D: no generation), then leaves A and D tied at zero; the declared tie-break chooses A. The decision does not depend on which of the two measured speeds is used, and it does not depend on the shared-generation convention: if C and M reuse B's one generation pass, A, C, D and M all sit at zero and A still wins the tie.
unmeasured: deterministic assembly and validation wall clock per cell was not instrumented on this checkout. It is CPU-side and small against 19,672 s of generation, but it is not zero and is not claimed to be; D's validator pass is the only part of it that is expected to be visible, and it is not measured here.
no_dollar_figure: no price basis is declared, so no $/1000 number is published; the receipt records this file's unit verbatim rather than labelling seconds as dollars
effect_on_the_ladder: rung 5 becomes the deciding rung; rung 2 stays failed at kappa 0.578 and rung 3 stays descriptive, so the shipped cell is A because it is the cheapest measured writer, not because it won a content comparison

signature.note: sign unit, tie-break acceptance and date; until then this file is a proposal and the receipt built from it is marked AWAITING_SIGNATURE
